questions.q: A ball is thrown up vertically with a certain velocity so that, it reaches a maximum height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math>. questions.solution:
The maximum height of a projectile thrown vertically upward is given by, h=u22g.

⇒u=2gh

Using equation of motion with constant acceleration,

s=ut+12at2

⇒h3=2ght-12gt2

⇒gt22-2ght+h3=0

Solving the above quadratic equation we will get the times t1 and t2. ⇒t2t1=2gh+2gh-4×g2×h32gh-2gh-4×g2×h3=2gh+4gh32gh-4gh3=3+23-2

Thus, the ratio t1t2=3-23+2

At t=2 s,

questions.q: A body starts moving from rest with constant acceleration covers displacement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> in first <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> seconds and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> in first <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi></math> seconds. questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For the displacement S1 of the body, it can be written that

S1=12a(p-1)2   ...1

And, for the displacement S2 of the body, it follows that

S2=12a(p)2   ...2

If t be the required time, it follows that

S1+S2=12at2   ...3

Equations (1), (2) and (3) imply that

(p-1)2+p2=t2⇒t=2p2-2p+1 s

questions.q: A ball is released from a height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> be the time required to complete first half and second half of the distance respectively. Then, choose the correct relation between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>.

questions.solution:
As the body is dropped from a certain height h, its initial velocity will be zero.

For first half, h1=h2.

Using second equation of motion, s=ut+12at2

We have, h2=12gt12.

Time taken in travel first half of the height, t1=hg    ...1.

For total height h, using again second equation of motion,

h=12gt1+t22⇒t1+t2=2hg    ...2

From equation 1 and 2, 

⇒12=t1t1+t2

⇒1+t2t1=2

⇒t1t2=12-1

Thus, the relation is t2=2-1t1.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : A truck and a car moving with same kinetic energy are brought to rest by applying breaks which provide equal retarding forces. Both come to rest in equal distance.

Statement II : A car moving towards east takes a turn and moves towards north, the speed remains unchanged. The acceleration of the car is zero.

In the light of given statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and Statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The work done in stopping the car and the truck can be written as

W=Fx=∆KE

As both the car and the truck are moving initially with the same kinetic energy, after being stopped, they will have the same change of kinetic energy.

Also, they are stopped with the same applied force.

Hence, from the above equation, it can be written that they have the same displacement, i.e., x1=x2.

Acceleration is a vector quantity. As the direction of motion of the car is different in the two given situations, the acceleration of the car will not be the same.

questions.q:
Match Column-I with Column-II :

  Column-I (x-t graphs)   Column-II (v-t graphs)
A I
B II
C III
D IV

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
(A) Here, the slope dxdt≥0 is always increasing, and we know that the derivative graph of the parabola is straight line, so the graph of velocity-time is straight line with increasing slope.

(A - II)

(B) Here, the slope dxdt<0 and at t→∞,dxdt→0. As the slope is decreasing with time, so the graph of velocity-time will have negative velocity and positive slope.

(B - IV)

(C) Here, the slope dxdt>0 for first half and dxdt<0 for second half.

As the slope of displacement-time is positive constant in first half and negative constant in second half, so the velocity will be uniform positive and uniform negative value.

(C - III)

(D) Here, the slope dxdt=constant.

As the slope of displacement-time is positive constant, so the velocity will be uniform positive value.

(D - I)

questions.q: A particle of mass 10 g moves in a straight line with retardation 2x, where x is the displacement in SI units. Its loss of kinetic energy for above displacement is 10x-nJ. The value of n will be ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Acceleration can be written as, a=vdvdx.

Given: a=-2x(-ve sign is due to retardation)

Therefore,

vdvdx=-2x⇒vdv=-2xdx

Integrating both sides, we get

12vf2-vi2=-2x22=x2⇒12mvf2-vi2=mx2

⇒|ΔKE|=0.01x2=10x-2

Hence, n=2.
